content.title: Oscars 2026: No win for filmmaker Geeta Gandbhir, who secured two nominations in the documentary categories this year
content.text: Geeta Gandbhir is an Indian-American filmmaker and editor known for socially conscious documentaries that focus on justice, race, and civil rightsAt the 98th Academy Awards, there were many snubs and surprises like every year. One of the snubs was for filmmaker Geeta Gandbhir, who secured two nominations in the documentary categories this year for her films The Perfect Neighbor and The Devil Is Busy.**Best Documentary Short segment**The Devil Is Busy was nominated along with A_ll the Empty Rooms, Armed Only with a Camera: The Life and Death of Brent Renaud, Children No More: Were_ and Are Gone, and Perfectly a Strangeness. STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS ADIn the Best Documentary Feature category, Geeta Gandbhir’s The Perfect Neighbor competed against The Alabama Solution, Come See Me in the Good Light, Cutting through Rocks, and Mr. Nobody against Putin. But she lost the Oscar to Mr Nobody Against Putin makers.More from EntertainmentWho is Geeta Gandbhir?Geeta Gandbhir is an Indian-American filmmaker and editor known for socially conscious documentaries that focus on justice, race, and civil rights.Before gaining recognition as a director, Gandbhir worked extensively as an editor on several acclaimed projects, including the HBO documentary series When the Levees Broke, for which she won a Primetime Emmy Award.Over the years, her work has consistently explored issues affecting marginalised communities, using documentary filmmaking as a tool to examine systemic inequality and real-life stories that often go unheard.At the 98th Academy Awards in 2026, Gandbhir made history by securing nominations in two different documentary categories in the same year.A historic Oscars momentWith nominations for The Perfect Neighbor and The Devil Is Busy, Gandbhir joins a small group of filmmakers recognised in multiple documentary categories in the same Oscars year.Her work highlights how documentary cinema can address pressing social issues while bringing deeply personal stories to a global audience, making her one of the most significant voices in contemporary nonfiction filmmaking.GamesView AllEnd of ArticleEnd of ArticleSwag bags, caviar and A-list fashion… The real cost of the OscarsThe 98th Academy Awards cost $56.9 million to host, with major expenses including the live show, red carpet installation, security, and lavish after-parties. Nominees and the host receive a luxury gift bag worth $350,000, featuring vacations, beauty treatments, and high-end products. The Oscars generate significant revenue, with $2 million ad spots and a $170 million boost to Los Angeles' economy, while winners see increased earnings and film sales.More Quick ReadsNext ArticleDivya Dutt’s 'Chiraiya' series: Marital rape is not considered a criminal offense in India, though the damage is invisible yet deepDivya Dutt’s 'Chiraiya' series: Marital rape is not considered a criminal offense in India, though the damage is invisible yet deepChiraiya is a 6-episode on JioHotstar. The series centers around Kamlesh (Divya Dutta), an ideal daughter-in-law whose life turns into a moral battle when her new sister-in-law, Pooja (Prasanna Bisht), reveals she is being sexually abused by her husband, Arun. The series shows marital rape and oppression behind closed doors. The problem of marital rape is that it is very difficult to prove it and everything apparently looks fine, but what happens behind closed doors that nobody really gets to know. Chiraiya shows how decades of social conditioning makes marital rape look normal. Marital rape is harmful for mental health Psychotherapist from Mumbai, Padma Rewari says, "The deepest damage is often invisible. Anxiety, self-doubt, and a fractured sense of self that lingers long after the moment has passed. It undermines mental wellness, particularly in environments where women are denied a voice where silence is expected, and pain remains unseen." She explains that marital rape doesn’t just break boundaries—it can quietly break a woman’s sense of safety, identity, and mental well-being from within. Marital rape laws in India According to reports published on CNN, marital rape is not considered a criminal offense in India, as of October 2024. The exception in §375 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC)—retained in the new Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)—states that sexual acts by a husband on his wife (over 18) are not rape, despite legal challenges over its constitutionality. Sadly, marital rape is considered to be crime only when the couple is legally separated. Advocate and activist Abha Singh who is currently practising in the High Court of Judicature at Bombay explains why marital rape is not considered a criminal offense: “The logic behind this is that it is very difficult to prove whether it is enjoyment of conjugal rights or it is something else. But there are laws to protect women in the country. If a woman is facing abuse or harassment, nothing stops her from walking out of the house or the marriage. If it is a case of domestic violence and she wishes to live in the same house, the husband can be stopped from entering her room. There can be something called judicial separation. Most importantly, I feel it is very difficult to prove in the court of law.” About Chiraiya According to the review published in Firstpost, the show is based in the heartland of India, where rivers and regressiveness co-exist, of course under the ghastly garb of progressiveness. And the traditional balderdash that threaten to ruin lives and shake foundations. And just like what we saw in the 2016 courtroom drama Pink, it’s time women’s NO exuded power and triumph. We have seen marital rape in films before, one of the recent ones being Luv Ranjan’s Akaash Vaani. The depiction has come back but this time more meticulously as it’s a show as opposed to a film. One wedding night is all what it takes to change everything. Dutta, who leads the show with a commanding screen presence, is established as wicked, who later transforms into a woman with steel, standing by a lady who has been raped on her wedding night. (With added inputs from agencies)Next ArticleDhurandhar 2 faces plagiarism allegation: Filmmaker Santosh Kumar RS claims script was copied calls Aditya dhar 'chindi chor'Dhurandhar 2 faces plagiarism allegation: Filmmaker Santosh Kumar RS claims script was copied calls Aditya dhar 'chindi chor'Just as Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge continues its record-breaking run at the box office, the Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge has landed in fresh controversy. Filmmaker Santosh Kumar RS has accused the makers of copying his script, claiming the similarities are too significant to ignore. “It’s hurting me”: Filmmaker alleges idea theft Santosh Kumar RS has alleged that the Ranveer Singh-starrer closely mirrors a script he had written in 2023. According to him, the core plot, narrative structure, and key elements of the film bear resemblance to his work. Expressing his distress, the filmmaker said the situation has been “hurting” him, as he believes his original idea has been used without credit or permission. According to a report in HT, he said, “You all might have watched Dhurandhar 2. It is working very well everywhere. After watching the movie, I came to know that it is my script and story. I had written it with a lot of hard work in 2023. I had narrated it to many companies because I was told that if I need big actors in the film, there has to be a corporate organisation backing it.” Claims of prior sharing and industry access The filmmaker further claimed that his script had been circulated within industry circles, raising the possibility that it may have reached the Dhurandhar 2 team during development. The same report mentions that Santosh had pitched the script to several major production houses, including Sony Pictures, Zee Studios, T-Series, and Dharma Productions, while attempting to mount the project with a larger cast. He added that he had envisioned Aditya Roy Kapur for the lead role. He also added, “I tried a lot, and I had sent my story to many people. I am a member of the Screenwriters Association, and I registered my story there in November 2023.” Legal action on the cards Santosh Kumar RS has stated that he is preparing to take legal action against the makers of the film. He has vowed to pursue the matter formally, indicating that the dispute could soon escalate into a courtroom battle. “I am putting a case on this movie because even though they have made a good movie, my story has been exploited. I had written the film for cinema and entertainment, but they made it as political propaganda. It is hurting me,” he said, adding, “What happened with me should not happen with anyone, and that's why I will put my maximum effort to let people know about it.” Writer Director Santosh Kumar RS accuses Aditya Dhar of being a "Chindi Chor".. Says, he had written the script as a cinema entertainment back in 2023 but Aditya Dhar stole it and showed it as a Political Propaganda.. Dhurandhar pic.twitter.com/LkgIZCDkM5 — D (@Deb_livnletliv) March 31, 2026 As of now, there has been no official response from director Aditya Dhar or the film’s lead star Ranveer Singh regarding the allegations. Film continues strong box office run Despite the controversy, Dhurandhar 2 remains a massive commercial success, dominating both domestic and global box office charts and setting multiple records within days of release.Next ArticlePrince Harry vs British Tabloid privacy trial nears end: All you need to know about the casePrince Harry vs British Tabloid privacy trial nears end: All you need to know about the caseBritain's Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, arrives outside the The Royal Courts of Justice, Britain's High Court, in London on January 22, 2026, for the fourth day the trial in his case against a major UK newspaper group. Prince Harry and six others, including pop icon Elton John, accuse two tabloids of privacy invasions and unlawful information gathering, in the prince's last active legal case in his long-running crusade against some UK media. (Photo by Henry NICHOLLS / AFP)The outcome of Prince Harry’s high-profile legal battle against British tabloids may now depend heavily on the credibility of a private investigator, as closing arguments wrapped up at London’s High Court. Case centres on disputed investigator testimony At the heart of the case is investigator Gavin Burrows, who previously admitted to targeting Harry during his younger years. However, during the trial, Burrows claimed he never carried out unlawful activities for Associated Newspapers, publisher of the Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday. He further alleged that a statement attributed to him, claiming he had done “hundreds of jobs” for the paper, was fabricated and that his signature had been forged. The defence argued that this disputed statement had formed the backbone of the lawsuit. Claimants insist on ‘systematic unlawful practices’ Representing Harry and other claimants including Elton John, lawyer David Sherborne maintained that there is substantial evidence of unlawful information gathering. He alleged that the newspapers engaged in practices such as phone tapping, voicemail interception, and deception over two decades. The claimants are seeking substantial damages, with legal costs alone estimated at nearly £40 million. Defence calls allegations ‘preposterous’ Lawyers for Associated Newspapers strongly denied all allegations, describing them as “preposterous smears.” They argued that the articles in question were based on legitimate sources, including friends, aides, and publicists, and said many claims were filed too late. The defence also challenged the reliability of witnesses, calling the case overly reliant on inference rather than concrete proof. Harry recounts personal toll During the trial, Prince Harry spoke about the impact of media intrusion, saying it left him “paranoid beyond belief” and strained his personal relationships. He also said relentless tabloid coverage made life “an absolute misery” for his wife, Meghan Markle. Harry has long linked his stance against the press to the death of his mother, Princess Diana, and to what he describes as a toxic media culture. Final judgment pending Presiding judge Matthew Nicklin has reserved his verdict, stating that the judgment will take time and require detailed consideration following the lengthy trial. He said at the end of the trial, "The remaining task is, of course, now mine. Judgment will take some time. After a short break over Easter ... I will be working on the case and the judgment effectively full-time ... so I won't be doing anything else ... and I will be toiling away on the judgment." This case marks the final chapter in Harry’s long-running battle with the British press, following previous victories and settlements against other publishers. The ruling could have far-reaching implications for media accountability and privacy laws in the UK, especially in cases involving public figures.
